Accept: NASA supports NGC 5139 globular-cluster classification, Centaurus association, ~17,700 ly, roughly 10 million bound stars, >500 Hubble images spanning two decades, seven fast-moving stars, and compelling evidence for an intermediate-mass-black-hole candidate. Accept: NASA supports Tarantula/30 Doradus/NGC 2070 names, emission-nebula classification, Dorado association, LMC context, ~170,000 ly, and young stars' UV/hot-particle flows producing the gas cavity and compressed ridges.

Accept: NASA TESS supports NGC 104/47 Tucanae as a globular cluster of hundreds of thousands of stars in Tucana and its apparent position above SMC. NASA APOD supports ~13,000 ly vs ~210,000 ly and that they are not physically close; the self-check asks which is nearer.

Accept: NASA supports Polaris near the north celestial pole, small 24-hour apparent circle, Little Dipper handle tip/Ursa Minor, not brightest star, ~26,000-year precession and approximate Vega epochs. The self-check tests both pole relation and long-term change.
